bib.title: Execution-Based Evaluation for Open-Domain Code Generation
bib.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2023

read.skipped: Numeric appendix tables (5-23) skimmed; figures are images. Reference list skimmed.

question: How well do code LLMs perform on natural, open-domain (library-using) NL-to-Python queries when judged by executing human-written tests?
hypothesis: Prior execution benchmarks are closed-domain, so models may behave differently on open-domain queries (implied; not stated as a formal hypothesis).
contributions: ODEX, first open-domain execution-based NL-to-Python dataset (945 pairs, 79 libraries, 1,707 tests, 4 natural languages)
Analysis of Codex and CodeGen on open vs closed domain
Comparison of execution vs five execution-free metrics and ablations on prompts and test counts

method.summary: Annotators wrote tests for 945 NL-code pairs from CoNaLa and MCoNaLa (StackOverflow), wrapping snippets into functions, adding imports, and writing mock/bounding/specialized-equality tests. Codex and CodeGen were evaluated zero-shot with pass@k.
method.task: NL-to-Python code generation with execution-based evaluation

datasets.name: ODEX
datasets.size: 945 NL-code pairs (439 en, 90 es, 164 ja, 252 ru); 1,707 test cases; 505 open-domain, 440 closed-domain
datasets.source: CoNaLa and MCoNaLa (StackOverflow); license CC BY-SA 4.0
datasets.preprocessing: Snippets wrapped into functions named by post ID (f_3844801); library imports added; minimal NL/code corrections by annotators

inference.samples: up to 10 samples per problem (pass@1..10); single run; no seeds stated
inference.prompting: zero-shot: function context (imports, signature) plus docstring with NL intent; optional 1 or all test cases in docstring; few-shot N in {1,2,3} in ablation

other.function_name: post ID by default; ablations with constant or 4-word intent summary
other.prompt_text: No verbatim prompt text in paper; Fig 6 is an image (function context + docstring).

metrics.name: pass@k
metrics.definition: fraction of problems with at least one correct prediction within k samples

eval.protocol: Execute predictions on annotated tests; no significance tests; authors recommend significance testing for users.

results.claim: ODEX has 945 NL-code pairs over 79 libraries with 1,707 human-written test cases.
results.quote: ODEX has 945 NL-Code pairs spanning 79 diverse libraries, along with 1,707 human-written test cases for execution

results.claim: Best Codex model code-davinci-002 reaches 47.15 pass@1 on English problems.
results.setup: ODEX 945 problems, zero-shot docstring prompt, nucleus sampling top-p 0.95, temperature 0.8, max 512 tokens, no finetuning; English subset (439)
results.table: Table 4, row en, DAVINCI-002, column pass@1

results.claim: CodeGen-6.1B-mono pass@1 on English is 34.49, while davinci-001 is 33.62, so 6.1B matches the 175B model at pass@1.
results.setup: ODEX 945 problems, zero-shot docstring prompt, nucleus sampling top-p 0.95, temperature 0.8, max 512 tokens, no finetuning; English subset; not so at higher k (davinci-001 pass@10 67.43 vs 43.05)
results.note: Text says 'similar pass@1 to the 176B CODEX DAVINCI-001'; Sec 4 says 175B.
results.table: Table 4, row en, 6.1B vs DAVINCI-001, column pass@1

results.claim: Open-closed pass@1 gap for davinci-002 ranges from 4.34 points (Spanish) to 38.57 (Japanese).
results.setup: ODEX 945 problems, zero-shot docstring prompt, nucleus sampling top-p 0.95, temperature 0.8, max 512 tokens, no finetuning; open = uses any library (built-in or third party), closed = none
results.quote: ranging from 4.34 in Spanish to 38.57 in Japanese on the best DAVINCI-002 model

results.claim: Model upgrades C1 to D1 to D2 do not always shrink the gap; it grows in English and Japanese.
results.quote: Gaps slightly shrink in Spanish, but increase in English and Japanese.

results.claim: CodeGen gaps shrink with scale (about 6.3 points in English from 2.7B to 6.1B) while Codex gaps rise by 4.9 points on average going to davinci-002.
results.quote: the gaps reduce by about 6.3 points in English and 1.7 points in Spanish

results.claim: CodeGen gaps are smaller than Codex gaps by 6.0 points on average.
results.quote: smaller than CODEX gaps across all languages, by on average 6.0%

results.claim: davinci-002 gets about 50% pass@1 on common libraries like random and math but under 10% on matplotlib and tensorflow.
Adding one test case to the prompt helps clearly; more adds little.
results.quote: injecting as few as one exemplar test case significantly improves the execution accuracy, yet adding more cases has little bonus

results.claim: Evaluating on one random test instead of all tests barely changes davinci-002 pass@1 on the full set (en 48.31 vs 47.15).
results.setup: davinci-002, no tests in prompt, full dataset (avg 1.8 tests per problem)
results.table: Table 21, rows 1 vs n, en, column @1

results.claim: On examples with 3+ test cases, one random test overstates pass@1: en 60.7 vs 52.7 with all tests, es 64.7 vs 47.1.
results.setup: davinci-002, subset with at least 3 tests (112, 17, 25, 45 examples en/es/ja/ru)
results.note: Sec 7 text says one test 'largely preserves' accuracy; the subset table shows 8 to 17.6 point drops. Subsets are small (17 to 112).
results.table: Table 22, row 1 vs n, columns en, es

results.claim: Execution-free metrics rank Codex models differently and BLEU barely separates passed from failed samples.
results.setup: davinci-002 predictions; BLEU, ROUGE-L, METEOR, ChrF, CodeBLEU
results.quote: Figure 10 shows negligible variances in BLEU scores of passed and failed groups.

results.claim: StarCoder (16B) pass@1 on English is 44.67 with open 37.00 vs closed 53.11, a gap also seen in models without SO training data.
results.setup: StarCoder, StarCoderBase, SantaCoder; same zero-shot protocol assumed
results.note: Decoding settings for these models not separately stated; inferred same as main.

results.claim: Annotators' canonical solutions pass 100% of annotated tests.
results.quote: the pass rate for all canonical code solutions over their annotated test cases is 100%

results.quote: Most samples, 53.4%, use at least one library.

limits: Execution safety needs inspection for open-domain code and tests.
Language coverage bounded by StackOverflow forums.
Small dataset (human effort); authors urge significance testing; ODEX suited to downstream evaluation or few-shot.
Possible train-test overlap of SO posts with closed models; mitigated by edits and StarCoder/SantaCoder check.
Average 1.8 tests per problem; test sufficiency argument rests on one-vs-all ablation.

terms.definition: code that entails library usage (both built-in and third-party); closed domain has none
